ITQAN:v4p336/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p336/r4.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v4p336/r4.claim: Al-Raghib says the final scripture gathers the fruit of earlier scriptures, whose laws were partly superseded and partly completed by Muhammad's law.
ITQAN:v4p336/r4.anchor: وقال الراغب إن الله تعالى كما جعل نبوة النبيين نبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم مختتمة

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r7.claim: “Upright books” describes the sheets: they contain written matters that stand straight, speak truth, and convey sound rulings and admonitions.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r7.anchor: {فيها كتب قيمة} صفة لصحف أي في تلك الصحف أمور مكتوبة

BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r8.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r8.claim: Al-Mufradāt takes the verse to point to the meanings of God’s books: the Qurʾan gathers the fruit of earlier scriptures.
BURSEVI:v10p375#2/r8.anchor: وفي "المفردات" إشارة إلى ما فيه من معاني كتب الله فإن القرآن مجمع ثمرة كتب الله المتقدمة

QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.claim: The Messenger is apposition to the proof; the purified pages are tablets of celestial intellects and souls, reached through detachment and free of natural, material, and human corruption, containing enduring, just foundations of the true religion.
QASHANI:98:2-8/r1.anchor: بدل من البينة أي: الحجة القائمة الواضحة

QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r4.claim: The upright books are straight and contain no crookedness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p439/r4.anchor: فيها كتب قيمة } : مستوية ليس فيها اعوجاج

IBNASHUR:98:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:3/r1.claim: Qayyimah means upright and sound: uprightness metaphorically conveys perfection and correctness, like something standing ready for beneficial work; its opposite is crookedness.
IBNASHUR:98:3/r1.anchor: والقيِّمة : المستقيمة ، أي شديدة القيام الذي هو هنا مجاز في الكمال والصواب

IBNASHUR:98:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:98:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:98:3/r2.claim: The feminine form of the adjective treats the described collective as a group.
IBNASHUR:98:3/r2.anchor: وتأنيث الوصف لاعتبار كونه وصفاً لجمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r3.claim: The phrase ‘in them are upright books’ omits a genitive construction: ‘in them are the rulings of upright books’; qayyima means established and just, guiding people fairly, in an intensive form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p507#4/r3.anchor: فيه حذف مضاف تقديره فيها أحكام كتب وقيمة:

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r1.claim: The pages contain just, upright verses that distinguish truth from falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r1.anchor: كتب قيمة أي عادلة مستقيمة تبين الحق من الباطل وهي الآيات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r2.claim: Muqatil says they are called books because they collect many different subjects.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p196#3/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل وإنما قيل لها كتب لما جمعت من أمور شتى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.claim: Ubayy had questioned Ibn Masʿud’s differing recitation; the Prophet affirmed both, and Gabriel then conveyed permission to recite in up to seven modes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r2.anchor: كان قد أنكر على إنسان، وهو: عبد الله بن مسعود، قراءة شيء من القرآن على خلاف ما أقرأه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that the Prophet recited this surah to Ubayy to communicate, confirm, and warn him, rather than to learn or review it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p455/r3.anchor: قرأها عليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قراءة إبلاغ وتثبيت وإنذار، لا قراءة تعلم واستذكار، والله أعلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir says the purified pages contain just, upright books without error because they come from God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r5.anchor: كقوله: {في صحف مكرمة مرفوعة مطهرة بأيدي سفرة كرام بررة} [عبس: 13 -16]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the books as upright and balanced.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p456/r7.anchor: قال قتادة: {رسول من الله يتلو صحفا مطهرة} يذكر القرآن بأحسن الذكر،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p535#3/r1.claim: Kutub qayyima are upright or just books.

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r5.claim: Qayyima means enduringly upright and derives from qāma; riḍā opposes displeasure and relates to past or future, while will relates only to the future.
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r5.anchor: والقيمة: المستمرة على جهة الصواب، وهي فيعلة من قام بالأمر يقوم به: إذا أجراه

JISHUMI:v10p7497/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r7.claim: Qayyima qualifies an omitted “religion” or “law”; it is feminine either to agree in meaning with milla or as an intensive suffix, with a poetic example for the semantic feminine.
JISHUMI:v10p7497/r7.anchor: (قيمة) نعت لمحذوف، تقديره: دين الله القيمة، أو الشريعة القيمة؛ لذلك أنث،

KASHSHAF:98:3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:3/r1.claim: The writings are upright and speak with truth and justice.
KASHSHAF:98:3/r1.anchor: { فِيهَا كُتُبٌ } مكتوبات { قَيِّمَةٌ } مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق والعدل

KASHSHAF:98:3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:98:3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:98:3/r2.claim: Their dispersal means turning away from truth, or splitting into factions: some believed, some denied, and some recognized it but stubbornly resisted.
KASHSHAF:98:3/r2.anchor: والمراد بتفرقهم : تفرقهم عن الحق وانقشاعهم عنه

MAJAZ:v2p306/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p306/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p306/r2.claim: Kutub qayyima are upright, just books.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r11.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r11.claim: The upright books are God's sound scriptures, whose truth the Quran mentions and confirms.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r11.anchor: أحدهما : يعني كتب الله المستقيمة التي جاء القرآن بذكرها , وثبت فيه صدقها , حكاه ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r12.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r12.claim: Alternatively, the upright books are God's just obligations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p315#3/r12.anchor: الثاني : يعني فروض الله العادلة , قاله السدي .

MUQATIL:98:1-6/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r4.claim: The upright writings are a straight book of truth without crookedness or disagreement; it is plural because the Qur'an contains many different subjects.
MUQATIL:98:1-6/r4.anchor: يعني كتابا مستقيما على الحق ليس فيه عوج، ولا اختلاف

NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#3/r1.claim: The written contents are in the scrolls and are upright, speaking with truth and justice.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p351#3/r1.anchor: مكتوبات ﴿ قيمة ﴾ مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق والعدل

NAHHAS:v5p271/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p271/r16.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v5p271/r16.claim: Ibn Zayd says the books in the scrolls are upright and balanced.

QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r4.claim: The books in the sheets are upright, straight, balanced, and firm, from the Arabic sense of standing straight.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r4.anchor: فيها كتب قيمة } أي مستقيمة مستوية محكمة من قول العرب: قام يقوم: إذا استوى وصح

QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r5.claim: Some scholars say that since sheets already mean books, kutub here means rulings; scriptural and Prophetic usage calls God's judgment His Book even when stoning is not written in the text, and a poem uses yaktubu for decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r5.anchor:
الكتب هنا: بمعنى الأحكام قال الله عز وجل:
كتب الله لأغلبن

QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r6.claim: Another view makes the books the Quran, pluralized because it includes several kinds of explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:98:2-3/r6.anchor: الكتب القيمة: هي القرآن فجعله كتبا لأنه يشتمل على أنواع من البيان

QUTB-ZILAL:98:3/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:98:3/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:98:3/r1.claim: Kitab can mean a subject or topic, as in chapters on purification, prayer, divine decree, and resurrection; the Qur'an's purified pages contain valuable topics and truths.
QUTB-ZILAL:98:3/r1.anchor: كما يقال كتاب الطهارة وكتاب الصلاة

RAZI:98:3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:98:3/r1.claim: One interpretation takes the books as verses written in the scriptures.
RAZI:98:3/r1.anchor: المراد من الكتب الآيات المكتوبة في الصحف

RAZI:98:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:3/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
RAZI:98:3/r2.claim: Ṣāḥib al-Naẓm says kutub can mean rulings, as in “God decreed,” and the hadith phrase “by God’s Book” means His ruling; the phrase can thus mean sound rulings.
RAZI:98:3/r2.anchor: الكتب قد يكون بمعنى الحكم : { كتب الله لأغلبن } ومنه حديث العسيف

RAZI:98:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI:98:3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says qayyima means straight and without crookedness, distinguishing truth from falsehood, as when a proof stands or becomes clear.
RAZI:98:3/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : مستقيمة لا عوج فيها تبين الحق من الباطل

RAZI:98:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:98:3/r4.claim: Another view understands qayyima as independently standing and conclusive in proof, from the phrase for carrying through an affair properly.
RAZI:98:3/r4.anchor: أن تكون القيمة بمعنى القائمة أي هي قائمة مستقلة بالحجة والدلالة

RAZI:98:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:98:3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:98:3/r5.claim: Though the Prophet was unlettered, reciting what is written in scriptures still counts as reciting their contents; a book attributed to Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says he read without writing, perhaps as a miracle.
RAZI:98:3/r5.anchor: إذا تلا مثلا المسطور في تلك الصحف كان تاليا ما فيها

SAMIN-DURR:98:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:98:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:98:3/r1.claim: Fīhā kutub may be a full sentence describing the scrolls or circumstantial to the pronoun in muṭahharah; alternatively, only the prepositional phrase is the modifier and kutub is its subject, which is best.
SAMIN-DURR:98:3/r1.anchor: وأن يكون الوصف أو الحال الجار والمجرور فقط،

STUDYQURAN:98:3/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r1.speaker: IK, Sh
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r1.claim: Upright books are error-free because they come from God.
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r1.anchor: Books upright indicates that they are free from errors and mistakes because they are from God

STUDYQURAN:98:3/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r2.claim: They distinguish truth from falsehood and contain no crookedness.
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r2.anchor: distinguishing between truth and falsehood with no crookedness therein

STUDYQURAN:98:3/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r3.claim: Their pages are honored, exalted, and purified.
STUDYQURAN:98:3/r3.anchor: they are on pages honored, exalted and purified

TAB:98:1/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:1/r9.speaker: author
TAB:98:1/r9.claim: The proof is the clarification that Muhammad is God’s messenger, who reads scriptures purified of falsehood; those scriptures contain God-given, just, upright books without error.
TAB:98:1/r9.anchor: ثم ترجم عن البيّنة ،   فقال :  تلك البينة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يقول :  يقرأ صحفا مطهرة من الباطل {  فِيها كُتُبٌ قَيّمَةٌ } يقول :  في الصحف

TAB:98:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:3/r9.speaker: author
TAB:98:3/r9.claim: The proof is the clarification that Muhammad is God’s messenger, who reads scriptures purified of falsehood; those scriptures contain God-given, just, upright books without error.
TAB:98:3/r9.anchor: ثم ترجم عن البيّنة ،   فقال :  تلك البينة {  رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفا مُطَهّرَةً } يقول :  يقرأ صحفا مطهرة من الباطل {  فِيها كُتُبٌ قَيّمَةٌ } يقول :  في الصحف

TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.claim: The proof clarifies Muhammad’s messengership; he recites pages purified of falsehood, containing just, upright divine teachings without error.
TAB-FULL:v24p551#2/r8.anchor: ثم ترجم عن البينة، فقال: تلك البينة، {رسول من الله يتلو صحفا مطهرة} [البينة: 2] ، يقول: يقرأ صحفا مطهرة من الباطل

TAB-FULL:v24p554#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p554#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p554#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd explains “upright” in both occurrences as straight and balanced.
TAB-FULL:v24p554#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {كتب قيمة} [البينة: 3] {وذلك دين القيمة} [البينة: 5] قال: " هو واحد؛ قيمة: مستقيمة معتدلة "

TABATABAI:98:1-3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r5.claim: Kutub may refer to writing, its medium, the words or meanings inscribed, or rulings and decrees; scripture uses ‘written’ for obligatory rulings.
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالكتب التي في الصحف الأحكام والقضايا الإلهية

TABATABAI:98:1-3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r6.claim: Qayyima means preserving and caring for a matter; the divine rulings are upright because they sustain society, guard its interests, and secure its well-being.
TABATABAI:98:1-3/r6.anchor: فإنها من القيام بالشيء بمعنى حفظه ومراعاة مصلحته وضمان سعادته

TABRISI:98:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:1/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:98:1/r5.claim: Qayyima means upright and consistent in what is correct. Hanif means inclined toward the truth; an alternative derives it from uprightness and calls a slanted foot hanif as a hopeful inversion.
TABRISI:98:1/r5.anchor: والقيمة المستمرة في جهة الصواب والحنيف المائل إلى الصواب والحق

TABRISI:98:3-5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:3-5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:98:3-5/r1.claim: The scripture pages contain straight, just books without distortion that distinguish truth from falsehood.
TABRISI:98:3-5/r1.anchor: أي مستقيمة عادلة غير ذات عوج تبين الحق من الباطل

TABRISI:98:3-5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:3-5/r2.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:98:3-5/r2.claim: Purified pages means the Quran, free of falsehood, lies, and slander; pages refers to their written contents, although the Prophet recited from memory rather than a book.
TABRISI:98:3-5/r2.anchor: عن الباطل والكذب والزور يريد القرآن عن قتادة

TABRISI:98:3-5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:3-5/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:98:3-5/r4.claim: The Quran itself contains the upright books by encompassing earlier scriptures, as shown by its confirmation of what preceded it; whoever recites it recites those books.
TABRISI:98:3-5/r4.anchor: إن القرآن يشتمل على معاني الكتب المتقدمة فتاليها تالي الكتب القيمة

TABRISI:98:3-5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:98:3-5/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:98:3-5/r5.claim: Alternatively, the Quran contains several kinds of knowledge, each kind being a book; al-Suddi says its rulings are just.
TABRISI:98:3-5/r5.anchor: معناه في القرآن كتب قيمة بمعنى أنه يشتمل على أنواع من العلوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says the books are truthful.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r1.claim: Muqātil says the books are straight, without crookedness or contradiction; they are called books because they contain many different matters mentioned in the Qurʾān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r1.anchor: وقال (¬4) (مقاتل: كتب مستقيمة ليس فيها عوج ولا اختلاف، قال:) (¬5) وإنما سميت كتبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r2.claim: They are upright and without crookedness, setting truth apart from falsehood clearly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r2.anchor: (وقال أبو إسحاق: كتب مستقيمة غير ذات عوج؛ تبين الحق من الباطل على الاستواء (¬7))

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r3.claim: Al-Qayyima means the standing, just one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: القيامة القائمة العادلة (¬1).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r4.claim: Qayyima can mean firm and sound, from standing straight as a proof stands; it can also mean something that administers affairs properly, hence books of sound rulings and arguments.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r4.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: (قيمة) مستوية محكمة؛ من قام يقوم إذا استوى، وصح من قولهم: قام الدليل على كذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r5.claim: Qayyima may describe a standing authority over a people, as in the hadith that a people whose manager is a woman will not prosper.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث: "ما أفلح قوم قيمتهم امرأة" (¬7)، فيكون المعنى: كتب قيمة بالأحكام والحجج.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r6.claim: The first sense, upright books, is more apparent and is the commentators' view because the alternative requires supplying an omitted word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r6.anchor: والقول الأول أظهر، وهو قول المفسرين (¬8)؛ لأن هذا الثاني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r7.claim: Kutub here means the verses written in the pages; alternatively it could mean judgments, as in 58:21 and the hadith about judging by God's book.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p211#3/r7.anchor: ومعنى الكتب في قوله: {كتب قيمة} هو الآيات المكتوبة في الصحف.

WAHIDI-QT:98:3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:98:3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:98:3/r1.claim: The books contain rulings that are upright and just.
WAHIDI-QT:98:3/r1.anchor: { فيها كتب } أحكام { قيمة } مستقيمة عادلة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r5.claim: The books contain rulings that are upright and just.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:98:1-6/r5.anchor: فيها كتب } أحكام { قيمة } مستقيمة عادلة

ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r1.claim: Razi says qayyimah carries an aggregate connotation in this context.
ASAD-NOTES:98:1#n2/r1.anchor: This aggregate connotation is inherent in the adjective qayyimah as used here (Razi)

ASAD-NOTES:98:7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:98:7/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:98:7/r2.claim: The sound ordinances and moral law are shared by all God-inspired messages, with the Qur’an as their final and most perfect expression.
ASAD-NOTES:98:7/r2.anchor: common to all God-inspired messages, of which the Qur'an is the final, most perfect expression

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.claim: The reading that includes People of the Book who also held explicit or implicit shirk best fits verse 3, which names only them.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r3.anchor: Üçüncü âyette yalnız ehl-i kitab zikrolunmasına bu mâna daha akrebdir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r14.claim: The sheets contain upright, stable books: enduring true writings, namely the Qur’an’s sheets and surahs commanded to be recited with iqra’.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r14.anchor: onlardadır bütün kütüb-i kayyime yani doğru sâbit kitaplar, bozulmaz, pâyidâr hak yazıları o temiz sahifelerin içindedir

ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.claim: Before a messenger, people could not fully know or unite upon true monotheism and could be excused; after the proof came, the People of the Book had no excuse for persisting in disbelief.
ELMALILI:98:1-4/r15.anchor: öyle bir beyyine gelmedikçe tamamen hak ve tevhid dinini bilip de birleşecek ve hâllerini değiştirecek bir vaziyette bulunmuyorlardı ve bunda mâzur olabilirlerdi

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.claim: Razi frames the puzzle: if munfakkin means leaving disbelief and hatta marks an endpoint, the first verse implies conversion after the Messenger, while verse 4 says division followed the proof.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r2.anchor: Sonra infikâkleri ne şeyden, Allah teâlâ onu zikretmemiştir. Lâkin murad, bulundukları küfür hâlinden demek olduğu mâlumdur

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.claim: The preferred Keşşaf solution reads verse 1 as the disbelievers’ earlier pledge to stay in their religions until the promised Prophet Muhammad came; verse 4 reports their failure to keep that pledge.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r3.anchor: Birincisi ve en güzeli Sâhib-Keşşâf’ın telhis ettiği vecihtir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.claim: On that reading, they promised to unite in truth when the Prophet came but instead split and persisted in disbelief; Razi illustrates this with a sinner who increases sin after becoming rich.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r4.anchor: onlar o Peygamber geldiği zaman hak üzerinde ittifak ile bir kelimede toplanmak vaad ediyorlardı, sonra da haktan asıl ayrılmaları ve küfürde kararları o Resul gelince oldu

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.claim: A third proposal makes munfakkin refer to mentioning the coming Messenger’s virtues: they spoke of his merits before his arrival, then disagreed after he came.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r6.anchor: Üçüncüsü: Münfekkîn küfürden infikâke değil, beyyine olarak gelecek resûlün menâkıb ve fezâilini anmaktan[^12] infikâk etmedikleri mânasına olmalıdır

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.claim: A fourth proposal says that, after the Messenger came, the whole group no longer remained disbelieving because some believed and some did not, satisfying hatta’s implication of change.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r7.anchor: Çünkü mecmû‘u o küfürde kalmadılar, bazısı mü’min bazısı da kâfir oldular. Bu kadarı da ‘hattâ’nın medlûlüyle amele kâfîdir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.claim: A fifth proposal says the Prophet’s mission shook their prior certainty in inherited religions; some converted, while others divided through stubbornness despite recognizing their old religions’ weakness.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r8.anchor: Resûlullah ba‘s olununca alışmış yapışmış oldukları eski dinleri hakkındaki cezm ü itikadları mütezelzil ve evvelki fikr ü kanaatleri perişan oldu

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.claim: This proposal distinguishes infikak as detachment from something once clung to from tafarruq as dispersion, showing how the post-Prophet condition differed from the prior one.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r9.anchor: bir şeyin bir şeyden infikâki ona yapışmış iken kopup ayrılması demektir. Tefrika da dağılmaktır

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.claim: Razi transmits these five solutions but identifies the first as preferred; the author finds Keşşaf’s wording more subtle and compatible with several proposals.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r10.anchor: Râzî bu beş vechi hikâye ve beyan etmiş olmakla beraber kavl-i muhtâr birinci vecih olduğunu da ihtar eylemiştir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.claim: Abu al-Su‘ud and others follow the first solution but supply the prior state as the object: their pledge and resolve to believe and follow the last Messenger.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r11.anchor: Ebussuud ve daha birçokları da Keşşâf’ın birinci vechi üzerinde yürümekle beraber “infikâk”in müte‘allakını mukaddemâ üzerinde bulundukları şey

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.claim: The account says the People of the Book prayed for victory through the last Prophet and threatened Arab opponents that they would defeat them with him; later polytheists may have adopted the claim.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r12.anchor: Ehl-i kitabdan bu vaadin vukū‘unda şüphe yoktur. Hatta onlar onunla Allah’tan fütûhât diliyorlar

ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.speaker: Ebussuud
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.claim: They asked the People of the Book whether Muhammad was the figure named in their scripture, yet after his arrival the People of the Book disbelieved and divided.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#2/r13.anchor: Resûlullah hakkında gidip ehl-i kitaba soruyorlar

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.claim: The author finds his earlier explanation most apparent: before the decisive proof, people were in a state where they could not leave their inherited condition; after it, the People of the Book should have believed.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r1.anchor: bunu bu esas üzere, yani bulundukları hâlden infikâk mânasına olarak bâlâda îzah ettiğimiz diğer bir vech ile anlamak

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.claim: The pledge reading is awkward when extended to polytheists; reading the object as their religions or disbelief would imply they should depart from them, though the proof was sent for that purpose.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r2.anchor: Ancak bunu o vaad ve azm ile tefsir etmek Sûre-i Bakara âyetine muvâfık olsa da müşriklere teşmîli itibariyle biraz dolambaçlı geliyor

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.claim: Before Muhammad’s mission was a period of interruption when religions were corrupted, pagans and non-pagans mixed, and truth and falsehood could not be distinguished.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r3.anchor: Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden önceki zaman dinlerin tahrif ve teşvîşe uğradığı müşrikle gayr-i müşrikin karıştığı

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.claim: Given the rule that punishment does not come before a messenger, the interval is an excuse period without responsibility; before decisive proof, the default is to leave people in their existing state.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r4.anchor: Fetret zamanları ise وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًۭا hükmüne[^22] nazaran mes’ûliyet teveccüh etmeyen bir mazeret zamanı demektir

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.claim: Prophets are sent to illuminate truth and duty during such periods, distinguishing believers and disbelievers so accountability can apply.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r5.anchor: Ve beşeriyetin böyle hakk u bâtılı seçemeyecek bir fetret ve zulmet içinde kaldığı zamanlardır ki taraf-ı ilâhîden

ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.claim: Following the previous surah’s account of revelation’s wisdom, this surah explains the pre-Prophetic interval: before Qur’an and Messenger the disbelievers could be excused, but after proof, especially the People of the Book’s rejection and division, they deserved punishment.
ELMALILI:98:1-4#3/r6.anchor: Kur’ân’ın inzâliyle beyyine-i ilâhiye olan Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden evvel ehl-i kitabdan ve müşriklerden bulunan kâfirler bulundukları hâllerinden ayrılmamakta mâzur olsalar da, hak dini beyan eden bu beyyine geldikten sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r7.claim: The books in those pages are upright divine verses and rulings distinguishing truth from falsehood; the Qur'an may be so described because it includes earlier scriptures' rulings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:98:1/r7.anchor: dosdoğru, hakkı bâtıldan ayıran ilâhî âyetler ve hükümler bulunduğunu bildirmektedir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.claim: Al-Bayyinah complements al-Qadr: the Qur’an’s exaltedness is explained, and the People of the Book and Makkan idolaters rejected it from conceit, not genuine doubt, using demands for a sign as a pretext.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p399/r1.anchor: conceit and arrogance which led them to this attitude

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r6.claim: The pages must contain clear, unambiguous directives rather than assorted stories.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p403/r6.anchor: the written pages should not contain tales and stories from here and there

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r1.claim: Islahi reads kutub as directives of the sharīʿah, rather than merely books, in this verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r1.anchor: This word also means the directives of the shar ī‘ah . Here in this verse, it is used thus.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r2.claim: Qayyimah means straight, clear, and explicit; the people wanted explicit religious directives and resisted unrelated material.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r2.anchor: means “straight, clear and explicit.” In other words, they desired explicit directives

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r3.claim: Their demand for written sheets matching the stone tablets of the Torah is presented with biting ridicule.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p404/r3.anchor: their demand was that just as the ten commandments of the Torah

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r4.claim: The books within the pages are written texts, and qayyima means upright and speaking the truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p519/r4.anchor: فيها كتب: مكتوبات، قيمة: مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r1.claim: “In them are upright writings” is a second modifier or circumstantial clause for the pages; alternatively only the prepositional phrase modifies them and “books” is its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r1.anchor: فيها كتب قيمة صفة ثانية لصحفا أو حال من الضمير في صفتها الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r7.claim: “Books” means written contents, and “upright” means straight in their proclamation of truth; al-Taysir says they are prophetic scriptures confirmed by the Qur’an, as if contained in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r7.anchor: وبالقيمة المستقيمة واستقامتها نطقها بالحق وفي التيسير هي كتب الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.claim: An alternative identifies the messenger as Gabriel and the pages as angelic copies from the Preserved Tablet, but turning “pages” into revelation is weak; al-Alusi prefers Muhammad, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p201#2/r9.anchor: والأولى حمل الرسول على النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وهو المروي عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p204/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p204/r11.speaker: محمد بن الأشعث الطالقاني
ALUSI-FULL:v30p204/r11.claim: Al-Talqani reads “the upright religion” as the upright books, linked by the definite article to the books of verse 3.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p204/r11.anchor: دين القيمة أي الكتب القيمة فأل للعهد إشارة إلى ما تقدم في قوله تعالى فيها كتب قيمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r5.claim: The books within the pages are their written verses and rulings; upright means just and straight, without crookedness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p493#2/r5.anchor: فيها} أي في الصحف، {كتب} يعني الآيات والأحكام المكتوبة فيها، {قيمة} عادلة مستقيمة غير ذات عوج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.claim: The Prophet said God commanded him to recite this sura to Ubayy; when Ubayy asked whether he had been named, the Prophet said yes and Ubayy wept.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي: "إن الله تعالى أمرني أن أقرأ عليك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.claim: A variant from Qatada says the command was for the Prophet to recite the Qur'an to Ubayy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p497/r6.anchor: وقال همام عن قتادة: "أمرني أن أقرأ عليك القرآن

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:3-5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:3-5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:3-5/r1.claim: The scrolls contain upright writings that speak the truth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet says that whoever recites this surah will be with the best of creation at the evening resting place on Judgment Day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:98:6-8/r7.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة لم يكن الذين كفروا كان يوم القيامة مع خير البرية مساء ومقيلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r6.claim: The writings contain precious knowledge and are wholly upright because they speak truth without shirk or any kind of crookedness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p496/r6.anchor: هي في غاية الاستقامة لنطقها بالحق الذي لا مرية فيه ليس فيها شرك ولا عوج

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.claim: Ubayy reported that God ordered the Prophet to recite the opening of al-Bayyina to him, followed by statements identifying the true religion as non-polytheist hanifiyya and promising that good is not denied.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r1.anchor: إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك فقرأ علي

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.claim: A second Ubayy report presents an expanded recitation with explanations of upright religion, righteous deeds, the best and worst of creation, and the recompense of the God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r2.anchor: إن أقوم الدين الحنيفية مسلمة غير مشركة

DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas recalled the Prophet's saying that Adam would seek a third valley of gold after two, and that only dust fills his belly; God accepts repentance.
DURR-FULL:v8p586/r3.anchor: لو كان لابن آدم واديان من ذهب لابتغى الثالث

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.claim: Ubayy affirmed that the Prophet had taught him the disputed wording; Umar asked whether to enter it in the codex, and Ubayy did not forbid him.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r1.anchor: هكذا اقرأنيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, Ubayy quoted the two-valley saying, and Umar asked whether it should be written; Ubayy said he would not forbid it, while remaining unsure whether it was revelation or Prophetic speech.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r2.anchor: فكأن أبيا شك أقول من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو قرآن منزل

DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.claim: Qatada glossed منفكين as ceasing their state, the Bayyina as this Qur'an, and the purified pages as the Qur'an praised in the finest terms.
DURR-FULL:v8p587/r4.anchor: عن قتادة {لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب والمشركين منفكين} قال: منتهي عما هم فيه

ABUHAYYAN:98:3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:3/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:3/r1.claim: Kutub means written texts or scriptures.

ABUHAYYAN:98:3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:98:3/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:98:3/r2.claim: Qayyima means upright and speaking the truth.

ALUSI:98:3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r1.claim: The phrase in the pages is a second adjective of ṣuḥuf or a circumstantial clause linked to the pronoun in muṭahhara; alternatively, only the prepositional phrase modifies, with kutub as its subject.
ALUSI:98:3/r1.anchor: صفة ثانية لصحفاً أو حال من الضمير في صفتها الأولى

ALUSI:98:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r2.claim: If bayyina means the Prophet who clarifies truth, identifying the proof with him is straightforward; if it means proof, his qualities are miraculous, as al-Ghazali and al-Busiri indicate, alongside other manifest miracles.
ALUSI:98:3/r2.anchor: وإطلاق البينة عليه عليه الصلاة والسلام على المعنى الأول ظاهر وعلى المعنى الأخير باعتبار أن أخلاقه وصفاته

ALUSI:98:3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:98:3/r9.claim: Kutub means written contents and qayyima means upright, speaking truth. Al-Taysir says these are the prophets' books, confirmed by the Qur'an as though contained within it.
ALUSI:98:3/r9.anchor: والمراد بالكتب المكتوبات وبالقيمة المستقيمة واستقامتها نطقها بالحق

ALUSI:98:3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r12.speaker: بعض
ALUSI:98:3/r12.claim: Some take the Messenger as Gabriel and the purified pages as angelic copies from the Preserved Tablet; Al-Ālūsī rejects this and prefers Muhammad, as reported from Ibn Abbas, Muqatil, and others.
ALUSI:98:3/r12.anchor: وقيل المراد بالرسول جبريل عليه السلام وبالصحف صحف الملائكة عليهم السلام المنتسخة من اللوح المحفوظ

ALUSI:98:3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:98:3/r13.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI:98:3/r13.claim: Al-Wahidi calls this one of the Qur'an's hardest passages in syntax and interpretation: if both groups disbelieved before the mission, the apparent sense says the Messenger's arrival ended their disbelief, contrary to history and 98:4, which says the people of the Book split only after the proof came.
ALUSI:98:3/r13.anchor: حتى قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط أنها من أصعب ما في القرآن نظماً وتفسيراً

BAGHAWI:98:3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:3/r1.claim: The books within the pages are the written verses and rulings.
BAGHAWI:98:3/r1.anchor: { فيها } أي في الصحف { كتب } يعني الآيات والأحكام المكتوبة فيها

BAGHAWI:98:3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:98:3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:98:3/r2.claim: Qayyima means just and upright, without crookedness.
BAGHAWI:98:3/r2.anchor: { قيمة } عادلة مستقيمة غير ذات عوج

BAYDAWI:98:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:98:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:98:3/r1.claim: The books are sound, upright writings that speak the truth.
BAYDAWI:98:3/r1.anchor: { فيها كتب قيمة } مكتوبات مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق .

BIQAI:98:3/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:3/r1.claim: The books within the pages are valuable teachings so precious that they deserve to be written down.
BIQAI:98:3/r1.anchor: جمع كتاب أي علوم هي لنفاستها حقيقة بأن تكتب

BIQAI:98:3/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:3/r2.claim: These teachings are entirely upright because they state indisputable truth and contain no shirk or crookedness of any kind.
BIQAI:98:3/r2.anchor: أي هي في غاية الاستقامة لنطقها بالحق الذي لا مرية فيه

BIQAI:98:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:98:3/r3.claim: Before the proof, the People of the Book shared belief in the Prophet based on explicit glad tidings, and polytheists promised to follow a warner; when he came, they divided, with some believing and others disbelieving.
BIQAI:98:3/r3.anchor: فإذا أتتهم هذه البينة انفكوا ، وانفكاكهم أنهم كانوا مجتمعين قبل هذا ، أهل الكتاب يؤمنون بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما عندهم من البشائر الصريحة به

BIQAI:98:3/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:98:3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr presents the sūra as completing the preceding discussion: after the command to recite the clarifying Book and the honor of its revelation night, it identifies this as the scripture the Jews invoked against Arab polytheists.
BIQAI:98:3/r4.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : هي من كمال ما تقدمها ؛ لأنه لما أمره عليه الصلاة والسلام بقراءة كتابه

BIQAI:98:3/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:98:3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Jews had anticipated the promised Book and Messenger and expected to prevail through him, but when the promise became visible they were the first to reject him.
BIQAI:98:3/r5.anchor: هذا الكتاب هو الذي كانت اليهود تستفتح به على مشركي العرب ، وتعظم أمره وأمر الآتي به ، حتى إذا حصل ذلك مشاهداً لهم كانوا هم أول كافر به

BIQAI:98:3/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:98:3/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:98:3/r6.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr contrasts informed rejectors, condemned as the worst creatures, with formerly uninformed believers such as Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, whom God favored and made the best creatures.
BIQAI:98:3/r6.anchor: فرحم الله من لم يكن عنده علم منه كأبي بكر وعمر وأنظارهما رضي الله عنهم أجمعين ، وحرم هؤلاء الذين قد كانوا على بصيرة من أمره

IBNATIYYA:98:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies an omitted construct: the pages contain the rulings of upright books.
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r1.anchor: فيه حذف مضاف تقديره فيها أحكام كتب قيمة

IBNATIYYA:98:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r2.claim: Qayyima means upright and just, dispensing justice to people; it is an intensive form.
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r2.anchor: وقيمة : معناه قائمة معتدلة آخذة للناس بالعدل وهو بناء مبالغة

IBNATIYYA:98:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r3.claim: After describing the books as upright, the discourse turns to mention those from the two groups who believed.
IBNATIYYA:98:3/r3.anchor: فإلى { قيمة } هو ذكر من آمن من الطائفتين

IBNKATHIR:98:3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r1.claim: Ibn Jarīr says the purified pages contain divine books that are just and upright, free of error because they come from God.
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r1.anchor: قال ابن جرير : أي في الصحف المطهرة كتب من الله قيمة : عادلة مستقيمة

IBNKATHIR:98:3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the books as upright and balanced.
IBNKATHIR:98:3/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد : { فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ } مستقيمة معتدلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir conjectures that the doubt Ubay experienced prompted the Prophet to recite Surah al-Bayyinah to him as reassurance, since it includes the Messenger reciting purified pages containing upright books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: قلت: وهذا الشك الذي حصل لأبي في تلك الساعة هو، والله أعلم، السبب الذي لأجله قرأ عليه رسول الله

MAWARDI:98:3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:3/r1.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI:98:3/r1.claim: The upright books are God’s scriptures mentioned by the Qurʾān, whose truth it confirms.
MAWARDI:98:3/r1.anchor: أحدهما : يعني كتب الله المستقيمة التي جاء القرآن بذكرها ، وثبت فيه صدقها ، حكاه ابن عيسى

MAWARDI:98:3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:98:3/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:98:3/r2.claim: The upright books are God’s just obligations.
MAWARDI:98:3/r2.anchor: الثاني : يعني فروض الله العادلة ، قاله السدي

NASAFI:98:3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:98:3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:98:3/r3.claim: The teachings are upright and speak with truth and justice.
NASAFI:98:3/r3.anchor: { كُتُبٌ } مكتوبات { قَيّمَةٌ } مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق والعدل

QURTUBI:98:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:3/r1.claim: Qayyima means upright, straight, sound, and firm, from the Arab root q-w-m for becoming upright and sound.
QURTUBI:98:3/r1.anchor: أي مستقيمة مستوية محكمة ، من قول العرب : قام يقوم إذا استوى وصح .

QURTUBI:98:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:3/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
QURTUBI:98:3/r2.claim: Some ask how scrolls can contain books if the scrolls are themselves books; Qurtubi answers that kutub here means rulings, as in 58:21 where the phrase means God has decreed.
QURTUBI:98:3/r2.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العلم : الصحف هي الكتب ، فكيف قال في صحف فيها كتب ؟ فالجواب : أن الكتب هنا بمعنى الأحكام

QURTUBI:98:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:98:3/r3.claim: The Prophet's promise to judge by God's Book while ordering stoning shows that Book of God can mean God's ruling, although stoning is not written in the text.
QURTUBI:98:3/r3.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( والله لأقضين بينكما بكتاب الله ) ثم قضى بالرجم ، وليس ذكر الرجم مسطورا في الكتاب

QURTUBI:98:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:98:3/r4.claim: Qurtubi uses a poetic line about what God writes to support the sense of kutub as divine decrees or rulings.
QURTUBI:98:3/r4.anchor: وما ذاك قال اللّه إذ هو يكتب

QURTUBI:98:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:98:3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI:98:3/r5.claim: Another view identifies the upright books as the Qur'an, called books because it contains many kinds of exposition.
QURTUBI:98:3/r5.anchor: وقيل : الكتب القيمة هي القرآن ، فجعله كتبا لأنه يشتمل على أنواع من البيان .

TAB:98:2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:98:2/r11.speaker: author
TAB:98:2/r11.claim: The purified pages contain writings from God that are just and upright, without error because they come from God.
TAB:98:2/r11.anchor: في الصحف المطهرة كتب من الله قيمة عادلة مستقيمة ،   ليس فيها خطأ ،   لأنها من عند الله .

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r1.claim: The Cairo copy omits the section devoted to criticizing Abū ʿUbayda in “Notices on the Narrators’ Errors,” so the writer says its value cannot be assessed.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r1.anchor: «التنبيهات على أغاليط الرواة» ، ولكن القسم الخاص بنقد أبى عبيدة غير موجود فى نسخة القاهرة . ولهذا لا نستطيع أن نقول شيئا عن قيمة هذا النقد.

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r2.claim: Despite criticism, Majāz al-Qurʾān remained a foundational reference among scholars throughout the centuries.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r2.anchor: على أن «مجاز القرآن» على الرغم من الذي سدد إليه من نقد ظل بين الدارسين مرجعا أصيلا طوال العصور

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba relied on Majāz al-Qurʾān in al-Mushkil and al-Gharīb.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r3.anchor: فقد اعتمد عليه ابن قتيبة (- 276) فى كتابيه «المشكل» و «الغريب»

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r4.claim: Al-Bukhārī used it in al-Ṣaḥīḥ; the writer says a detailed study of his use is needed and postpones it elsewhere.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r4.anchor: والبخاري (- 255) فى «الصحيح» ، ويحتاج الأمر فى استفادة البخاري خاصة من مجاز القرآن إلى بيان وتفصيل أرجأت القول فيه إلى مكان آخر

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī relied on the book in his tafsīr, often discussing it and comparing its view with those of exegetes and scholars.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r5.anchor: وكذلك اعتمد عليه الطبري (- 310) فى تفسيره وأكثر من مناقشته ومقارنة رأيه بآراء أهل التأويل والعلم

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r6.claim: The writer notes al-Ṭabarī’s objections to Abū ʿUbayda in the footnotes to Majāz.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r6.anchor: وقد ذكرت فى حواشى «المجاز» اعتراضاته على أبى عبيدة

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r7.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazīdī and al-Zajjāj used the book in their works on Qurʾānic meanings.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r7.anchor: واستفاد منه أبو عبد الله اليزيدي (- 311) ، والزجاج (- 311) فى معانيه

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r8.claim: Ibn Durayd used it in al-Jamharah, al-Sijistānī in his Gharīb, and Ibn al-Naḥḥās in his Maʿānī al-Qurʾān.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r8.anchor: وابن دريد (- 321) فى «الجمهرة» وأبو بكر السجستاني (- 330) فى «غريبه» وابن النحاس (- 333) فى معانى القرآن

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r9.claim: Al-Azharī, Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, and al-Jawharī also drew on the book in their named works.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r9.anchor: والأزهرى (- 370) فى التهذيب وأبو على الفارسي فى الحجة (- 377) ، والجوهري (- 391) فى الصحاح

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayd al-Harawī and Ibn Barrī, among other earlier scholars, used it in their works.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r10.anchor: وأبو عبيد الهروي (- 402) فى الغريبين، وابن برى (- 582) فى حواشى الصحاح وغيرهم من المتقدمين

MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r11.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r11.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r11.claim: Among its important later users, Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī drew on Majāz in Fatḥ al-Bārī.
MAJAZ:v1p1#15/r11.anchor: ومن أهم من استفاد من كتاب المجاز من المتأخرين ابن حجر العسقلاني فى «فتح الباري»

BAQILLANI:v1p113/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r1.claim: Non-Arabs can recognize Qur’anic inimitability by learning that the Arabs were challenged and failed to produce its like; someone unable to master Arabic is even less able to meet that challenge.
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r1.anchor: قد بينا انه لا يتهيأ لمن كان لسانه غير العربية من العجم والترك وغيرهم أن يعرفوا إعجاز القرآن

BAQILLANI:v1p113/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r2.claim: An Arabic speaker without mastery of eloquence, styles, and linguistic forms cannot directly recognize inimitability and must rely on the same evidence as a non-Arab.
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r2.anchor: فهو كالأعجمي في أنه لا يمكنه أن يعرف إعجاز القرآن إلا بمثل ما بينا

BAQILLANI:v1p113/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r3.claim: A master of Arabic styles knows the limits of human eloquence and recognizes speech beyond human capacity, just as experts distinguish strong and weak examples within a genre.
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r3.anchor: فأما من كان قد تناهى في معرفة اللسان العربي ووقف على طرقها ومذاهبها

BAQILLANI:v1p113/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r4.claim: Like a money changer or cloth merchant, specialists discern qualities hidden from others; yet even experts may differ over which style they prefer.
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r4.anchor: وهذا يميز أهل كل صناعة صنعتهم فيعرف الصيرفي من النقد ما يخفى على غيره

BAQILLANI:v1p113/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r5.claim: Some experts prefer weighty, solid speech; others prefer flowing, graceful, readily understood language, while still others choose obscure meanings and rare diction over ease.
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r5.anchor: لأن من أهل الصنعة من يختار الكلام المتين والقول الرصين ومنهم من يختار الكلام الذي يروق ماؤه

BAQILLANI:v1p113/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r6.claim: ʿUmar praised Zuhayr for praising people only for qualities they possessed, then addressed ʿAbd Banī al-Ḥaṣḥāṣ after he recited a line saying that age and Islam restrain a man.
BAQILLANI:v1p113/r6.anchor: وروي أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وصف زهيرا فقال كان لا يمدح الرجل إلا بما فيه

DAMGHANI:v1p399/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p399/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p399/r12.claim: The ten senses listed for كتاب also include the Qur'an, Torah, Gospel, and obligation; this segment gives no examples for these last four senses.
DAMGHANI:v1p399/r12.anchor: ك ت ب على عشرة أوجه الكتابة الحساب اللوح عدة المرأة أعمال بني آدم الرزق والأجل القرآن التوراة الإنجيل الفرض
